narrative: The PR adds a per-voice language field and language-steered resolution. The reviewer's 35 findings were almost all correct, and the agent's choices were sound throughout, often improving on the proposed cure (constructor-level normalisation, gating narrowing under the substitution switch, sweeping audio alongside language). Fix-caused findings cluster on three patterns: a normaliser fixed at one reader or producer but not the others (F9 led to F12/F13/F21; F10 led to six duplicate piper threads), fixes that left comments or rationales describing the old behaviour (F24, F27), and fixes that shipped without the test that would pin them (F29's vacuous assertion, F33, F35). Round 3 consisted entirely of findings caused by round-2 fixes.
guidance_observations: Six round-1 threads were one finding, which shows that normalising at one producer (remote.py) instead of the shared constructor guarantees a sweep of findings on the other producers.

Several fixes were declared complete with a unit test on a helper while the symptom lived in an endpoint header; driving each fix's test through the endpoint would have closed F12/F13/F21 a round earlier.

The agent mutation-tested fixes from round 1 onward, but F29 shows the first test it added for a new 422 message was not mutation-checked; that check belongs on every new regression test, not only on later ones.
The agent's self-attribution was mostly accurate but over-claimed on F31, where the over-broad listing predated the review.
